title: Grateful Dead Live at Pirates World on 1970-03-24
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > Cass > DAT > ZA2 > CD Wave > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clean but oddly mixed soundboard capture of a stellar 1970 set highlighted by a soaring Dark Star, epic High Time and superb Weir jams on Good Lovin'.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean sound‑board source though the stereo split places most instruments on one channel and vocals on the other, giving it an unusual mix. Musically the show is praised as a gem of ’70, with standout performances of Dark Star, Good Lovin', High Time, The Other One, Lovelight and Me & My Uncle, plus inspired drumming and Weir’s exceptional guitar work. Overall the performance and song flow are described as creative, seamless and essential for any Deadhead.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise (mostly 4‑5 stars) for both the musical performance and the clean soundboard capture; minor mix quirks keep recording rating slightly below show rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall sound, but an unusual stereo split (most instruments on one channel, vocals on the other) and a few edit cuts (e.g., Morning Dew).

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers highlight creative segues—Lovelight into Me & My Uncle, jazzy drum jams into Good Lovin', and a fluid transition from High Time through Dark Star to The Other One—giving the concert an engaging, almost narrative flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for soulful, inspired playing (e.g., “Jerry put his soul in the music”, “finest playing yet”).
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir lauded for standout jams on Good Lovin' and a beautiful rendition of Cold Rain & Snow.
band_member_comments.Drums: Jazzy, creative drumming noted, especially early jam into Good Lovin' and strong drum breaks.
